paperName: The Operation of Markets and Market Failure

questions.questionText: Demerit goods represent a type of market failure because

options.text: their consumption results in positive externalities.
their production results in negative production externalities.
they are over-consumed in a free market.
they are under-consumed when left to free market forces.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sets of characteristics can best be used to distinguish between different market structures?

options.text: The concentration ratio and the income elasticity of demand
The ease of entry to the industry and the degree of product differentiation
The number of buyers in the market and the productivity of firms
The scale of production in the industry and the presence or absence of externalities

questions.questionText: The following diagram shows the production possibility frontier for an economy that produces bread and honey. If the economy is initially at point W, then the opportunity cost of moving to point X is

options.text: 6 units of honey.
8 units of honey.
12 units of bread.
23 units of bread.

extractionNotes: the question prints a diagram or chart (an image)

questions.questionText: Which one of the following gives a positive value for the cross elasticity of demand?

options.text: A fall in air fares increases the demand for holidays
A fall in the cost of car insurance increases the demand for cars
A rise in the price of petrol decreases the demand for cars
A rise in rail fares increases the demand for coach travel

questions.questionText: The following diagram shows the impact of a government subsidy for recycling waste which shifts the supply curve from S1 to S2. Which one of the following areas measures the cost of the government subsidy?

options.text: A B C P1
A B D P2
F C D E
P1 C D P2

questions.questionText: An economist puts forward a hypothesis which is assessed against evidence. As a result of this, the hypothesis is accepted, rejected or modified. This is an example of

options.text: how normative but not positive economic statements are tested.
how value judgements influence economic decision making.
the methodology used to test economic theories.
why economics is a social not a natural science.

questions.questionText: In economics, the ‘long run’ refers to the time period when

options.text: all factors of production are fixed.
all factors of production may change.
revenue is fixed.
some factors of production are fixed, others may vary.

questions.questionText: The growth of car manufacturing around Birmingham led to firms producing components for cars. As a result, car manufacturing firms experienced a fall in their average cost of production. This is an example of

options.text: a financial economy of scale.
a marketing economy of scale.
a technical economy of scale.
an external economy of scale.

questions.questionText: The equilibrium market price of a good increases. The establishment of the new equilibrium at a higher price would most likely result from

options.text: a fall in the price of a substitute.
a rise in the price of a complementary good.
excess demand at the original price.
new firms entering the market.

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the demand and supply curves for new houses. The initial demand and supply are D1 and S1. Other things being equal, which one of the following combination of events is most likely to cause demand and supply to shift to D2 and S2?

options.text: A fall in mortgage interest rates and a relaxation of planning restrictions
A fall in the price of new homes and a fall in the productivity of construction workers
A fall in the price of rented accommodation and a fall in the price of raw materials
A rise in incomes and a rise in wages of construction workers

questions.questionText: A government builds a new road to reduce traffic congestion on existing roads. This project would inevitably result in government failure if

options.text: local residents raised environmental objections to the new road.
the cost of the new road was twice as large as the original estimate.
the reduction in traffic congestion was smaller than forecast.
total benefits from the new road were less than the cost of the new road.

questions.questionText: A supermarket has estimated values of the income elasticity of demand for some of its products as shown in the table below. If incomes increase by 5%, for which of these grocery items will the quantity demanded increase by more than 1%?

options.text: Eggs
Fruit
Fruit and cheese
Milk and eggs

questions.questionText: In the diagram below, D1 and S1 are, in the absence of government intervention, the market demand and supply curves for a vaccine. The demand curve D2 shows how much of the vaccine would have been demanded if the external benefits could have been captured by the market. The diagram illustrates that there is a misallocation of resources because in a free market

options.text: the price of the vaccine is too high.
there is excess demand equal to (Q3 – Q1).
there is under-consumption of the vaccine equal to (Q3 – Q1).
there is under-production of the vaccine equal to (Q2 – Q1).

questions.questionText: In an economy, the median total household wealth was £218 400 whilst the median total household income was £32 100. Which one of the following can be concluded from the above statement?

options.text: A household with an income of £32 100 would be expected to have wealth of £218 400
Exactly 50% of the population had wealth higher than £32 100
The average household income was higher than the average household wealth
The average household wealth was nearly seven times the average household income

questions.questionText: If firms in an industry increase their spending on advertising, it is likely to

options.text: help firms to differentiate their products.
make it easier for new firms to enter the industry.
make the demand for the firms’ products more elastic.
reduce the monopoly power of the firms in the industry.

options.text: firms will experience diseconomies of scale.
the benefits from economies of scale will increase.
the market price falls and output increases.
the market price rises and output falls.
